title: MTEL Physical Education (22) Practice Test - MTEL - Pedagogy and Instruction
subject: MTEL

questions.q: In a physical education activity, elementary students work in pairs with a ball. First, partners face each other a few feet apart and gently toss the ball back and forth. Then the partners gradually move farther and farther apart, throwing and catching the ball until they are too far apart to throw or catch the ball successfully. This activity is most likely designed to promote student understanding of which of the following concepts?
options: level
speed
range
pathway
questions.explain: This activity directly teaches the concept of **range**, which is the distance an object is thrown. As students move farther apart, they must learn to apply more force to increase the range of their throw to reach their partner.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Once students demonstrate mastery of fundamental skills for rhythmic movement, it would be most appropriate to introduce them next to which of the following styles of dance?
options: freestyle dance
modern dance
contra dance
line dance
questions.explain: Line dancing is a good next step because it uses relatively straightforward, repetitive sequences of steps and doesn't require partner coordination. This provides structure for applying fundamental rhythmic skills before moving to more complex forms like modern or contra dance.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: A group of fourth-grade students are learning a creative movement pattern in which they form a line and perform a forward roll simultaneously. Each time they execute the roll, one particular student rolls in a crooked line and bumps into a neighbor. To address this problem, it would be most appropriate for the teacher to:
options: ask the student to remain after class so that the teacher can assess the student's attitude.
observe the student's roll to assess movement technique and provide individualized instruction.
change the choreography to create larger spaces between students when they execute the roll.
substitute an easier movement for the roll so all students will feel successful performing the routine.
questions.explain: The most likely cause of a crooked roll is improper technique. The teacher's best first step is to observe the student closely to identify the technical flaw and then provide specific, individualized feedback to help them improve.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: During a basketball activity, students work in pairs. Each student has a ball and faces his or her partner from several feet away. As one partner makes a two-handed chest pass, the other partner simultaneously makes a bounce pass. After a while, they switch passes. Which of the following is most likely the main objective of this activity?
options: developing skills in passing
practicing pick and roll skills
developing offensive footwork while passing
practicing passing around a defender
questions.explain: This drill involves the direct and repeated practice of two fundamental basketball skills: the chest pass and the bounce pass. The main objective is to improve the technique and accuracy of these passing skills.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: After a few lessons in the fundamentals of bowling, students practice at a bowling alley on a field trip. After the students select balls, the teacher reviews basic bowling skills with the students. Which of the following skills should be reviewed first in the sequence of skills?
options: learning to roll a hook ball
learning the five-step approach
rolling a straight ball
choosing a grip that is comfortable
questions.explain: The proper sequence of instruction starts with the most fundamental element. Before the approach or the roll, a student must have a comfortable and secure grip on the ball. This is the foundation for all other bowling skills.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: During an outdoor field day at the end of the school year, elementary students will participate in a variety of physical activities. Which of the following organizational approaches to the day's events is likely to be most effective in enhancing students' self-esteem and sense of self-worth?
options: ensuring that most activities emphasize coordination and balance rather than speed or strength
offering activities that allow students of varying fitness and skill levels to achieve individual success
including only activities that are cooperative rather than competitive in nature
recruiting responsible students and relying on them to help staff and run the activities
questions.explain: To promote self-esteem for all participants, a field day should offer a wide variety of activities. This allows every student, regardless of their specific strengths or skill level, to find something they can enjoy and succeed at.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: While outdoors, young elementary students practice estimating their heart rate as they walk, then jog, and then run through a simple obstacle course. Each time they complete the course, the students check their pulse for a few seconds and describe it as either slow, medium, or fast. This activity is particularly effective for:
options: familiarizing students with techniques for calculating respiration rates during aerobic activity.
promoting students' ability to distinguish between aerobic and anaerobic activity.
introducing students to basic cardiorespiratory fitness principles in the context of a physical activity.
encouraging children to improve their endurance and stamina in the context of a play activity.
questions.explain: This activity allows students to experience basic cardiorespiratory principles firsthand: physical activity increases heart rate, and different intensities of activity produce different heart rate responses. It's an age-appropriate introduction to a core fitness concept.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following Web sites provides access to an interactive, personalized system for assessing and monitoring one's current diet and physical activity levels on an ongoing basis?
options: USDA ChooseMyPlate
Consumer Reports: Health
WebMD
Healthy People 2020
questions.explain: The USDA's ChooseMyPlate.gov website offers interactive tools for planning, tracking, and analyzing diet and physical activity. Its personalized recommendations can be customized by age, gender, and activity level.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: When encouraging children to integrate healthy eating practices and patterns into their everyday lives, it is best to emphasize that healthy eating habits:
options: eliminate physical stress by stimulating growth hormone production.
reduce the need for rest and sleep, leaving more time for play and school activities.
help prevent both short- and long-term health problems such as colds, dental cavities, and obesity.
increase cardiorespiratory efficiency without exercise, leading to improved stamina.
questions.explain: To motivate children, it's effective to connect healthy eating to tangible short- and long-term benefits they can understand. Linking good nutrition to preventing problems like cavities and obesity makes the concept relatable and promotes positive lifelong habits.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: To address the developmental levels of middle and high school students, many secondary fitness education programs use a skills-based approach. In this type of approach, the main overall goal is to provide students with:
options: sufficient practice opportunities in one or two movement forms in order to develop high levels of proficiency in those areas.
an overview of how external factors (e.g., peers, family, media, environmental conditions) affect personal health and fitness.
the knowledge and strategies that are essential for improving fitness and maintaining lifelong physical activity.
information about how to locate, access, and use health-related resources.
questions.explain: A skills-based fitness education approach focuses on equipping students with the necessary knowledge and practical skills (e.g., how to monitor intensity, set goals, design a workout) to independently manage and maintain their physical activity and fitness throughout their lives.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: The goals of an elementary physical education program include promoting students' sense of self-worth and perception of physical competence, as well as fostering their appreciation and enjoyment of group and team games. These goals are specifically designed to address which area of student development?
options: social-emotional development
intellectual development
motor development
moral development
questions.explain: Goals such as promoting self-worth, enjoyment, and appreciation for group activities are central to fostering positive emotional health, self-perception, and interpersonal skills, which are all key aspects of social-emotional development.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following best describes a significant challenge in secondary physical education programs?
options: providing genuine field experiences for pre-service teachers seeking certification in physical education
providing adequate time and activities to encourage students to adopt a lasting ethic of physical activity
locating contemporary curriculum models designed to promote healthy and active lifestyles
distinguishing between physical activities for secondary programs and middle school programs
questions.explain: A primary goal of secondary P.E. is to instill lifelong fitness habits. A significant challenge is having sufficient class time and designing engaging, relevant activities that motivate adolescents to value and adopt physical activity as a permanent part of their lives.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: In a school–community collaboration, a local fitness facility agrees to offer high school students free passes to the facility after they receive related fitness instruction in a physical education class. Which of the following best describes a primary advantage of this type of collaboration?
options: Previewing the facility improves chances that students will continue to use it, which benefits both the facility and students.
The arrangement generates goodwill between the facility and local businesses owned by students' families.
The facility provides a less stressful environment for students who are self-conscious about body composition.
The collaboration allows physical education teachers to reallocate time usually spent on fitness to other instructional areas.
questions.explain: This collaboration removes barriers to access. By becoming familiar and competent with the facility in a structured school setting, students are more likely to use it independently, fostering lifelong fitness habits and providing potential future customers for the facility.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: While introducing students to an outdoor tag game called "Kick the Can," the physical education teacher says that the game probably originated in Great Britain in the mid-1800s. The teacher tells students that the same game is called "Burkuit" in Holland. The teacher also notes that in India, a similar game is called "Esha Desai," and that in Japan, a variation of the game is called "Kankai." Imparting this type of information to students is important primarily because it:
options: communicates that games are enjoyed by many cultures and played throughout the world.
reflects the teacher's awareness that the game might not be familiar to all students.
illustrates that physical education is an essential part of school curriculums in other countries.
demonstrates the teacher's facility with other languages, thereby strengthening relationships with students of diverse backgrounds.
questions.explain: Sharing the global history of a game helps students appreciate that play is a universal human activity. It connects them to other cultures and highlights similarities across the world, promoting cultural awareness.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: In a school district, physical education teachers work with central office technical staff to incorporate wellness technology into schools on a district-wide basis. The wellness technology includes the FITNESSGRAM®, ACTIVITYGRAM®, and MyDietAnalysis programs. This collaboration is likely to maximize the physical education program's effectiveness by:
options: providing parents/guardians and administrators with immediate access to fitness program accountability data.
eliminating the need for teachers to use additional forms of physical fitness wellness assessment techniques and tools.
establishing a networking system by which physical education teachers can easily communicate with students' families, faculty, and service providers.
providing students and teachers with immediate access to data and allowing students to design, monitor, and progress toward personal wellness goals.
questions.explain: These software programs empower students by giving them tools to track their own activity and diet, analyze the data, and set personal goals. This access to personal data fosters student ownership and self-management of their wellness.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following strategies is likely to be most practical and effective in advocating for and promoting the values of physical education programs?
options: encouraging teachers in other subject areas to integrate motor learning and movement science concepts routinely into instruction
assisting teachers and administrators in locating and accessing inexpensive fitness and recreational resources and facilities in the community
devoting equal amounts of physical education time and resources to developing students' cognitive, social, physical, and motor skills
using a variety of media and opportunities to communicate with students, families, and school community members about fitness and recreational resources and activities and their benefits
questions.explain: Effective advocacy involves clear, consistent communication. By using multiple channels (newsletters, websites, events) to inform the entire school community about the program's activities and benefits, a teacher can build broad understanding and support.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following practices is likely to be most essential for the smooth functioning of elementary physical education classes?
options: establishing and announcing to students time goals for each lesson activity
ensuring that there is a procedure in place for dealing with interruptions during class
preparing the activity space and having necessary equipment on hand prior to lesson activities
assigning students into teams or squads that remain intact over the course of a term or semester
questions.explain: Effective preparation is the key to a smooth lesson. Having the activity space set up and all equipment ready *before* students arrive minimizes downtime, maximizes activity time, and prevents management issues that arise from disorganization.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following best describes the core equity issues that are most important for physical education teachers to consider in designing appropriate instruction?
options: gender, individual differences in experience and skill level, and cultural relevance
NASPE content standards and definitions of a physically educated individual
authentic outcomes and alignment between instructional goals and assessment
prevailing values and economic forces in the sport and leisure industries
questions.explain: Equity in physical education means ensuring all students can participate fully and feel included. This requires a teacher to be mindful of and adapt instruction for differences in gender, prior experience, skill level, and cultural background.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: During an overhand throwing activity, a physical education teacher tells a student, "Great L-shape throwing the ball. Now try to take a longer step toward the target." This is an appropriate cue to help improve performance of a skill, primarily because it:
options: avoids the use of physical education jargon and motor learning terms.
defines the motor task in visual terms for the student and provides spatial directions.
challenges the student to go beyond what the student most likely perceives as his or her potential.
combines positive specific feedback with encouragement to correct one component of the skill.
questions.explain: This is an example of the 'feedback sandwich' method. It starts with positive, specific reinforcement ('Great L-shape'), provides a constructive correction ('take a longer step'), and reinforces the student's ability, which motivates further effort.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: During a lesson on kicking, the physical education teacher notices that some students fail to step forward with their kicking foot and leap onto their nonkicking foot just before the kick. Which of the following strategies would be most helpful in adapting this activity to address these issues?
options: Place a plastic cone in front of each student's dominant side and instruct students to step, leap, and kick without a ball, trying to skim the cone.
Sprinkle powder on the lower half of balls and encourage students to step, leap, and kick and then check the ball to see where their foot made contact.
Have students concentrate on a design element on the balls (e.g., a seam, a pattern, a label) to improve their focus and technique during the kick.
Place two poly spots at the desired distances in front of each student and instruct students to step on one and leap onto the other before contacting the ball.
questions.explain: Using poly spots as visual cues helps break down the complex sequence of actions. It clarifies the separate, discrete movements (step, leap) and their spatial relationship, allowing students to master the sequence before kicking.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following is a primary advantage of using commercially-prepared task cards when teaching physical education skills to students?
options: Teachers can be assured that students will demonstrate consistency in performing skills.
The cards can be quickly adapted for use as assessment rubrics in order to evaluate performance.
Students can refer to the cards as needed for written cues and visual images of proper techniques.
The information on the cards can be easily revised or rearranged to address specialized skills.
questions.explain: Task cards provide individualized, self-paced instruction. Their primary advantage is that students can refer to them whenever needed for visual and written reminders of correct technique, fostering independence and skill acquisition.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: The Internet is likely to be most useful to physical education students for which of the following research purposes?
options: locating appropriate resources for individual physical activities and nutritional needs and guidelines
finding information on the manufacturers of various fitness products and equipment
estimating the number of universal games that exist in various countries under different names
comparing the advantages and disadvantages of various physical fitness regimens
questions.explain: The Internet is an excellent tool for finding information on local resources (parks, trails, fitness centers) and for accessing reliable guidelines on nutrition and weight management from reputable health organizations.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following is a significant advantage of using formative assessment strategies?
options: They provide teachers with feedback about student progress and help identify areas of strength and weakness.
They provide standardized data that captures the degree to which students have achieved learning outcomes.
They allow comparisons to be made between individual students and between groups of students.
They are useful for providing documentation to parents/guardians, administrators, and stakeholders related to program effectiveness.
questions.explain: The key purpose of formative assessment is to monitor learning *during* the process. It provides immediate feedback to the teacher about what students are understanding and where they are struggling, allowing for timely adjustments to instruction.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Physical education assessment strategies are likely to be most effective when careful planning is done to ensure that assessments:
options: are presented in written formats that are familiar to students.
achieve an equal balance between informal and formal instruments.
utilize consistent directions and testing conditions.
are aligned with student outcomes and instructional frameworks.
questions.explain: For an assessment to be effective and valid, it must directly measure the learning objectives and student outcomes that were the focus of instruction. Alignment ensures that you are testing what you have taught.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Playing a "Simon Says" activity with kindergarten students would be an appropriate strategy for a physical education teacher to use to evaluate students' ability to follow directions and to:
options: distinguish among locomotor skills.
demonstrate body awareness concepts.
use effective balancing skills.
differentiate personal space from general space.
questions.explain: A game like 'Simon Says' is excellent for assessing body awareness in young children. By giving commands like 'Simon says touch your nose,' the teacher can observe if students can identify and move various body parts.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following assessment strategies would be most appropriate for assessing student progress in mastering a new motor task?
options: conducting observations of the student's performance of the task in familiar practice or game situations
evaluating the student's technique by interviewing the student about how he or she feels while performing the task
determining whether the student has progressed from the cognitive stage of motor learning to the associative stage
assigning the student a writing task to check whether he or she can describe how to perform the motor task
questions.explain: The most authentic and accurate way to assess mastery of a physical motor skill is to directly observe the student performing that skill in a real-world context, such as a practice drill or a game.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: When using standardized, norm-referenced assessment software to assess physical education students, it is most important to ensure that:
options: test administration procedures are flexible.
the testing instrument employs a standard multiple-choice format.
test items correspond to specific levels of the psychomotor taxonomy.
the demographic characteristics of the norm group are similar to those of the group being tested.
questions.explain: A norm-referenced test compares a student's score to a 'norm group.' For the comparison to be fair and meaningful, the group of students being tested should have similar demographic characteristics (e.g., age, socioeconomic status) as the norm group.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following practices is most important to use in conference discussions with parents/guardians about the performance of physical education students?
options: assuring parents/guardians that all physical education instruction is developmentally appropriate
addressing student strengths and achievements in addition to areas needing improvement
asking parents/guardians whether their child's progress in physical education meets their expectations
describing in detail the assessment tools and techniques used to evaluate student performance
questions.explain: A productive parent-teacher conference should provide a balanced picture of the student's performance. Highlighting strengths and achievements alongside areas for improvement gives a complete view and fosters a positive, collaborative tone.
questions.subject: MTEL

questions.q: Which of the following is considered an unethical practice according to professional codes of conduct for physical educators?
options: using classroom observations, checklists, or other types of informal assessment data to inform or revise instruction
discussing health-related implications of a body mass index or skinfold measurement with a student's parent or guardian
using a physical education assessment tool or test for a purpose for which it was not designed or validated
presenting aggregate or group fitness test results rather than individual student data to illustrate the need for fitness resources
questions.explain: It is unethical to use an assessment for a purpose other than its intended, validated use. For example, using a fitness test score (designed to assess health) to determine a student's grade (meant to assess learning) compromises the validity of the assessment and is an improper application.
questions.subject: MTEL
